versions.notes: Original paper text. Two separate Rule 0 paragraphs existed (tileset rule, character deck rule); Rule 25 was a third, later setup paragraph. Superseded by v1.1.0 which merges all three.

data.text:
Rule 0 (Initial setup tileset rule): The standard 3x4 tileset from the deck of the effects, depose two cards face down in each field. Depose on each tile one creature or one skill card at random. Randomly depose two class cards over the tiles occupied by monsters.

Rule 0 (Initial setup character deck rule): For each player
- Draw two character cards, choose one and discard the other (Your character card enters the tileset).
- Deal 10 effect cards and 4 skill cards: You may put any of them in your deck and the rest in your archives.
- Deal 2 class cards: discard one and put the other one initially on board over your face up archive column.
- Draw as many Attack, Block / Move / Posture cards as you want to create a deck of minimum 15 cards.

versions.notes: Folded Rule 25 into Phase A of this rule on 2026-10-19 per author decision; Rule 25 is now superseded. Author-written text used verbatim.

data.text:
Rule 0 (Initial setup: tileset rule and character deck rule).

Tileset. Over a tile-set 3x4 (4x4 or 5x5, depending on the count of the players):
- First distribute two effects on each tile as traps.
- Then shuffle the monsters and skills cards in one pile and distribute at random one more card of them over each tile.
- Finally each player may choose its starting entry point in order determined by the Will stat. Every next player cannot choose a location that is nearby any other non-ally player. Remember that you cannot choose an entry point that has a monster (green) card deposed already, and you still have to resolve the entry point traps.
Then you choose on which trap to depose your character clockwise, starting with the character with the highest Will (the character is counted as a Move action, and you may play Instants during this action). The player puts his character on a tile at least two tiles away from the enemy. If you put your character on a monster-occupied tile, you are in immediate combat with it: apply the effects as traps and put them face up on that tile simulating the monster's hand.

Character deck.
- Draw two character cards, choose one and discard the other (your character card enters the tileset).
- Deal 10 effect cards and 4 skill cards: you may put any of them in your deck and the rest in your archives.
- Deal 2 class cards: discard one and put the other one initially on board over your face-up archive column.
- Draw as many Attack / Block / Move / Posture cards as you want to create a deck of minimum 15 cards.

logic.description: Setup of a Dimension and of each player's deck. Tileset side depends on the player count (3x4 for up to 2 players, 4x4 for 3, 5x5 for 4 or more); every tile receives two face-down effects as traps and then one more card drawn from the shuffled monsters+skills pile. Each player draws 2 character cards and keeps 1, is dealt 10 effects and 4 skills (any of them may go to the archive instead of the deck), is dealt 2 class cards and keeps 1 (placed face up as the class permanent), then tops the deck up with A/B/M/P cards to at least 15 cards. Entry points are chosen in descending Will order; an entry tile may not hold a monster, may not be adjacent to a non-ally, and must be at least 2 tiles from any enemy; entering counts as a Move action (instants allowed) and the entry tile's traps still resolve. The engine evaluates these counts at turn 0 before the first action.

data.text: Each character has three actions (turns) per round chosen from Attack, Block, Move, Posture. Monsters have their own action count written on the card; monsters with four actions per round force the player to replace one action with Empty Posture. A player may decide which round to enter the Dimension tileset; permanents may be cast outside the dimension so their effects are ready on the entry tile.

logic.description: Turn economy. A character has exactly 3 actions per paper round (one engine turn), each chosen from Attack, Block, Move, Posture (or Empty Posture / Empty Move, Rule 6). A monster uses the action count printed on its card, 1 to 4; when an opponent has more actions than you, the surplus actions on your side are forced Empty Postures (and a forced EP may not be turned into an Empty Move). A player may delay entering the tileset and may cast permanents outside the Dimension so they are ready on the entry tile. The engine stores actions_per_round on every unit and derives the forced-EP count from the difference.

data.text: Once a tile is Attacked or Moved towards, it turns face up and becomes 'open'. If there is a creature there, it awakens. If there are only effects there, the tile is a trap set with 20 power for each element used in the effects. All effects on the tile activate once as traps.

logic.description: Discovering a tile. A face-down tile turns face up ('open') the moment a unit Attacks it or Moves towards it. If a creature lies there it awakens (Rule 3) and the tile's effects become its hand. If only effects lie there the tile is a trap: every effect fires once against the discoverer with a power of 20 per element (pc ruling), i.e. trap power = 20 x number of trap elements; an element whose power does not exceed the defender's stat fails (Rule 18) and one failing element fails its whole effect (Rule 4). Context fields: tile.open, tile.creature, tile.effects (entry ids), tile.effect_elements (all elements of the trap effects).

The creature is steered by the next enemy player in seating order (the player after the one in contact). data.text: To disable a trap, at some point all the effects on it must fail to kill you (you survive the damage) or fail to lock you (because of high stats). It is enough for one element of an effect not to work for the whole effect to fail. If a trap or monster kills or locks your character, you lose one time and may re-enter the Dimension once again fighting for a draw (Remi). All traps are resolved in one round.

logic.description: Trap resolution. A trap (open tile with effects and no creature) is disabled once all of its effects have failed to kill or lock the discoverer: the discoverer survives the damage and is not locked. An effect fails as a whole as soon as one of its elements fails, i.e. when the trap power (20 per element, Rule 2) does not exceed the defender's stat behind that element. All traps resolve within one round. A kill or lock costs the character one re-entry attempt (a 'time'); the character may re-enter and fight for a draw.

prerequisites.description: An open tile with effects and no creature is a trap.

effects.description: The trap is disabled when the caster survived and is not locked after all effects fired.

data.text: Each monster in contact with a character typically throws 4 D6 to determine its current action: green=Block, blue/white=Move, red=Attack, black=Posture. Some monsters have custom patterns (BAAPM, AAAM) and throw those D6 combinations each action. When the Posture score is highest, the monster may choose the proper effect from its hand and skips throwing dice until all the effect's elements are emitted.

logic.description: Monster actions by dice. A creature in contact with a character rolls 4 D6 per action (or its printed pattern such as BAAPM / AAAM, one die per letter) and acts on the colour that scores highest: green = Block, blue/white = Move, red = Attack, black = Posture. When Posture wins the creature picks an effect from its hand and stops rolling until all of that effect's elements are emitted (one per action). Context: caster is the creature, caster.dice_pattern its optional printed pattern, die_face the winning colour, cast.step/of the running emission.

data.text: If the hero cannot or does not want to act, they play an empty action called Empty Posture. Empty Posture does not grant Posture's benefits (does not beat Move). Effects may still be made during Empty Posture. The Empty Posture card may alternatively be played as Empty Move (declared first). For combat calculations, the enemy chooses which empty-type to treat it as (Posture enemy picks Empty Move; Attack enemy picks Empty Posture). The Empty Posture card always returns to the hand after action evaluation.

logic.description: Empty Posture / Empty Move. EP is the no-op action: it gains no matrix edge (pc: 'EP no benefits'), may still emit an element, and always returns to the hand. The same card may be declared first as Empty Move: the unit advances halfway toward its target (ceil(dist/2) hexes). For the resolution matrix the enemy picks the empty type that hurts the empty actor: Attack treats EP as Posture (A vs EP = 2), Posture treats EP as Empty Move (P vs EP = 1), Block treats EM as Move (B vs EM = 1); Move/Block vs EP are neutral. A forced EP (Rule 1/7) may not be converted into EM. Reaver exception (pc): its EP and EM fight as Attack.

prerequisites.description: The caster declared Empty Posture or Empty Move.

data.text: Characters act simultaneously each turn (cards face-down). Sequence: (1) all characters/creatures in contact put their cards face down each turn; (2) cards flip face up and actions resolve — instants and skills may still be played before resolution; target is pointed out and damage is attempted. Characters/creatures in contact may play effects on their Posture or Empty Posture actions. After the final turn of a round, characters may discard remaining cards and draw up to five. Monsters do not discard. If an opponent has more actions per round than you, you may be forced to play Empty Posture (it cannot be converted to Empty Move when forced).

logic.description: Turn structure. Units in contact commit their action cards face down simultaneously each action; cards flip, instants and skills may still be played, targets are pointed out and the resolution matrix applies: base 1 damage for Attack plus 1 per edge (A>P/EP, P>M/EM/EP, M>B, B>A), so A vs P = 2 and B vs A = 1 to the attacker. Effects are emitted only on P/EP. After the third action of the engine turn, characters may discard and draw up to 5 (Rule 10); monsters never discard. A unit facing an opponent with more actions per round fills the gap with forced Empty Postures.

data.text: Each action within the round the player declares in order: (1) Empty Move (special way of playing Empty Posture — move halfway toward target, declared first); (2) turn up an action card (A/B/M/P/EP); (3) play Effects — effect declaration binds the current action to emit a specific element (first as ordered in effect description). There is NO stack — all skills and effects apply; if some effect/skill prohibits an action or emission it is applied finally as a replacement; (4) play skills / instants / class-card per-round abilities, OR point-buy an element/color to try to destroy a token.

logic.description: Declaration order within an action: (1) Empty Move, (2) the action card (A/B/M/P/EP), (3) effects — a declared effect binds this action to emit its next element, (4) skills, instants, class abilities OR a point-buy against a token (Rule 24). There is no stack: everything applies, prohibitions are applied last as replacements. Pc override: instants are committed with the action; if the action's maths gave the player no benefit (took no less, dealt no more, healed no more than without the instant) the instant returns to the hand instead of being discarded, in bonus rounds too (rule_8_instant_returns). Context: outcome.{took_with, took_without, dealt_with, dealt_without, healed_with, healed_without}.

data.text: A character may leave used cards in the archive instead of discarding (for deck refinement). Defeated monsters also go to the deck archive and may be used by effects like necromancy, summoning (substituting for a random library creature), possess, link — as outer-dimension allies. data.text: Played cards go to the discard pile. A permanent-type card goes in front of the deck until destroyed; you must point-buy (roll dice summing ≤ your stat; place the highest die as a defense token with that color; you may repeat the roll if unhappy). Place over the permanent a small neutral die with value equal to the lowest color value. Tile token = big colored die placed to the right side of the tile (character card is a rectangle), set by point-buy, adds as a bonus to each creature on the tile. Permanent token = colored die positioned over a specific stat on the character card, applied as stat bonus. Stat penalty token = wooden die, same rule but placed below the stat number and subtracted.

logic.description: Permanents and tokens. A small neutral die over the permanent shows the lowest colour value. Token kinds: tile token (big coloured die right of the tile, bonus to every creature there), permanent token (coloured die over a stat, added), stat-penalty token (wooden die under a stat, subtracted), shield token (Rule 20). Context: card (effect id), dice (the roll), permanent.tokens.

versions.notes: Unified from the three prior Rule 14 entries (acquisition/trade, life, adjacency) on 2026-10-19 per author decision.

data.text:
Rule 14 covers three closely-related mechanics.

Part A — Acquisition / trade. Acquiring effects/skills happens via conquering a field with an effect, or obtaining one from a defeated character's deck. Place the acquired card in discard or archive pile. You may spend an action to trade archives with an adjacent character if one of you moves towards the other. With an adjacent hero you may also discard your cards into their discard pile, or place a just-played card in their discard pile instead of your own.

Part B — Life. Life of each creature/character = Σ Stats ÷ 10, rounded at mathematical principle (see Rule 21). All characters have Σ Stats = 40 → 4 life tokens. Monsters have varying Σ Stats (e.g. Dragon = 80 → 8 life tokens). Damage by effect is rounded at the same principle when the effect is cast. The total life token is a small neutral die, recalculated whenever damage is done or a new token of any kind of value ≥ 5 is added/updated over the tile or character.

Part C — Adjacency. Characters can be attacked only by another character or creature in the 8 surrounding tiles (horizontal, vertical, diagonal).

logic.description: Rule 14 in three parts. A — acquisition/trade: effects and skills are acquired by conquering a tile or from a defeated character's deck and go to discard or archive; adjacent characters may trade archives for an action when one of them moves towards the other, and may discard into each other's piles. B — life: life = round_half_up(sum of stats / 10) (life_from_stats): every character has 40 -> 4, a Dragon 80 -> 8; the life die is recalculated whenever damage is taken or a token of value 5 or more is added to the tile or character. C — adjacency: a unit may only be attacked from the surrounding tiles (paper: 8 neighbours; engine: hex distance 1, in_contact).

prerequisites.description: Trade and attacks need the units in contact.

effects.description: Part B: life from the stat sum, rounded half up at the nearest ten.
Part C: the defender can be attacked only when in contact.
Part A: archives may be traded when adjacent and one side moves towards the other.
Part B: the life die is recalculated when a token of value 5+ sits on the unit.

data.text: With every action the hero can target a field (Move) and/or an enemy (Attack/Move). Block does not target; it deals 1 damage to each enemy who attacked you. Empty Posture cannot perform targeting with effect or skill. If two characters target the same tile for a Move: only the one actually using Move moves there; on mirrored actions no one moves. Using Attack, you MAY follow (optional) the targeted hero if they move, as if performing a Move targeting the enemy's tile. You may also stay on your tile if you target the enemy/tile with Attack/Move (e.g. channeling an effect via point-buy).

logic.description: Targeting. Attack and Move target one enemy or tile; Posture and Block are untargeted (pc), Block dealing 1 to each enemy who attacked you (B > A edge). Pc target priority when no explicit target: (1) the enemy against whom I take less damage, (2) an enemy that would take damage, (3) the enemy with the lowest life; a right-clicked target is honoured when in contact. Score = 100 x i_take_less + 10 x enemy_takes_damage - life, highest wins. Two units Moving to the same tile: only the one truly using Move arrives; on mirrored Moves nobody moves. An attacker may follow a target that moves away. Context: candidate.{i_take_less, damage_to_enemy, life}, caster.move_target, defender.move_target.

data.text: To cast, elements are emitted via contiguous Postures — one Posture emits one element in order. If the sequence is interrupted the cast fails. After casting, the effect goes to discard unless it is a Channeled or Permanent effect. Channeling may continue as long as the character stays on the same tile (uses environment to channel). Casting a permanent effect places it in front of the deck. Instant effects are the exception (see Rule 20). Postures must be contiguous — a two-element effect cannot be cast with Posture → Block → Posture.

data.text: Effect types: Point-buy — damage done via point-buy rather than stat-emit comparison. Damage — summarized damage by stat comparison per element spent. Instant — castable with any action, not only Posture. Shield token — add point-buy as colorless die (rounded up) in the emitted color over the tile; acts as tile-based extra life, cumulative. Non-Damage / Instant effects — put a value-1 die in the emitted element color over the castable card until cast or the condition expires. Point-buy mechanic — roll dice summing ≤ stat, keep highest. Apply as defense token / stat penalty by color on permanent/character/tile, OR as damage if the effect is Damage type. If sum exceeds stat (fail), you can repeat next action as a contiguous action (slower casting). Channeling — continuously cast the same effect next turn(s), even next round, as temporary permanent with point-buy defense tokens. Goes to discard when you stop channeling or when the last defense token is destroyed. Stat buy — effects summarize points spent to emit elements until some total is reached across multiple rounds.

logic.description: Effect types and the point-buy. Types (valid_effect_types): damage (Rule 21 stat comparison), point-buy (dice, unresistable), instant (any action), shield token (die over the tile as extra life, cumulative), channeling (temporary permanent, lost when channeling stops or its last token dies), stat buy (bank the stat per emission until the card's total, stat_buy_paid). Point-buy: roll point_buy_dice_count(stat) d6; the roll fits when the sum is at most the stat (point_buy_succeeds); keep the highest die (point_buy_token_value) as token or damage. Pc: the point-buy is per emission and a failed roll re-emits only that element next action; once a non-instant effect is picked only P/EP/EM remain selectable; Fireball deals delta damage and leaves a fire tile token; Force Shield is permanent and its Vitality die is subtracted from the effect sum. Context: dice (this roll), cast.non_instant_selected.

data.text: If the effect does Damage, the difference in Stats (yours − enemy's) per element equals the stat damage. The effect's Stat Damage is divided by 10 and rounded at mathematical principle (round-half-up), calculated each turn for completed effects when the defender has no tokens to destroy (defender chooses which token is destroyed). Example 1: fire delta 3 + water delta 2 = 5 points → rounded up to 10 → 1 damage. Example 2: instant effect does 2 points, then 2 more next action = 4 points → rounded down to 0 → 0 stat damage.
data.formula: damage = round_half_up(sum_of_stat_deltas / 10)   // 0.5 rounds up, 0.4 rounds down

logic.description: Effect damage. For a completed damage effect, per element take max(caster stat - defender stat, 0), sum, divide by 10 and round half up (0.5 -> 1, 0.4 -> 0; resolved contradiction: not a ceiling): fire 3 + water 2 = 5 -> 1 damage; 2 + 2 = 4 -> 0. Damage applies when the defender has no tokens left to destroy; otherwise the defender chooses a token to lose instead. Pc Dodge: 1 less combat damage in total. Implemented as rule_21_delta_damage; life uses the same rounding (life_from_stats).

data.text: Different effects can be cast simultaneously as long as they require the same elements. data.text: A fortress building has a stat of 30 to 60 (its stat type and value come from its hex) and blocks the way. A unit within 1 hex of it may, once per action, stat-buy it: a Posture / Empty Posture emission of that stat banks the unit's current stat (no roll). Once the bank reaches the fortress stat the fortress breaks and is consumed (gone for everybody), and the breaker point-buys round(stat / 10) dice: the highest die becomes a permanent bonus stat token on that stat of their character, just like the one Artifice makes (one per element: it replaces an earlier one only if higher). It is destroyable like any bonus token: an adjacent enemy emitting that stat destroys first the permanents, then the character bonus tokens (this one), then the tile bonus tokens, with a point-buy die at least the token value. The token lasts until it is destroyed that way or its owner dies (it is not kept when a saved game is loaded).

It counts in my stat, my life maximum (Σ/10 rule) and the UI token modifier like any stat token, and falls under Rule 24: an adjacent enemy emitting that stat against me takes my permanents first, then my character stat bonus tokens (this one), then the bonus tile tokens under me (rule24Order); a die ≥ the token value destroys it. Snapshot: fortress_bank_json { id, stat, value, bank, turn, action }; the old fortress_bonus_json is no longer written (ignored if an older peer sends it). Another unit breaking it voids my bank. Lifetime (user ruling 2026-11-15: "permanent token from the highest die"): the token is permanent — no turn / round / action end, snapshot rebuild or later token of that element that is not higher takes it; only Rule 24 (as above) or my death removes it (peer.mjs DIED branch drops my Fortress tokens; a Resurrect does not bring them back); tokens are not kept when a save is loaded. The breaker gets a HUD notice with the dice and the token. data.text: Every monster holds 6 effect cards in its deck besides its 11 action cards and 4 skills: the 4 effects printed on its creature card (deck_effects — a thematic mix of 2 damage effects, 1 defensive one and one more, all cheap enough for its stats) and 2 random effects from the library, fixed for that monster when it enters the dimension. They circulate like any card (draw, hand, discard pile; the one it drops at death may be one of them). Once awake the monster casts them with Posture / Empty Posture emissions like a player: a damage effect when an enemy is in its reach, a defensive one when an enemy is near, a control effect on an enemy in contact; it keeps emitting until the cast is done and does not move while casting (moving would interrupt it, Rule 19). It only casts what its stats can pay for; a card it cannot use goes back to its discard pile when its hand holds no action card. Allied bots (npc heroes of a team, companions, summons) cast the effect cards of their own deck the same way (no cards are added to their decks): they also heal the most hurt ally in contact with Turn Life, brew Potion Brew on a hurt or weaker ally in contact, cast slightly costlier cards than monsters (every element stat at least 8, delta damage mean at least 12, a heal judged on its Vitality), and cast Meteor Shower only when it hits more enemies than their own side, themselves and their owner included.

They circulate like any card (draw, hand, discard, reshuffle; dropDeathCard may drop one). npcPlan (once awake): a cast in progress goes on with Posture / Empty Posture, never a move (Rule 19), aimed at the nearest enemy; else npcCastChoice over the hand — damage on an enemy within the effect's reach (delta only if it hurts), defence with an enemy within threat_range, control on an enemy in contact, Meteor Shower only when more enemies than allies are within 10 and life ≥ 3 — each with chance cast_chance[kind] from the monster's own RNG; otherwise the old weighted A/M/P/B pick. data.text: A monster's natural effect (its creature card's innate effect; most monsters have one, some none) is a Permanent card. Every monster with one enters the dimension with 2 copies of it already cast as permanents, power 6 each, held in its permanents holding (they count toward the 15-card deck floor); no further copy is in its deck and it never casts it. The two copies are separate permanents: Rule 24 destroys them one at a time (a die of 6 of the stat of the effect's elements) — each destroyed copy goes to the monster's archive, out of circulation — and the effect lasts until both are gone. Natural effects stay monster-only (players keep casting Creation and Spirit Link as their own cards). While they stand: Earthquake hits every enemy in contact at the end of each turn; Creation bars enemies with less Matter from the hexes next to the monster; Spirit Link links the monster to its nearest allied creature (both copies standing = ∀: all four stats; one copy: Vitality); Love / Awe — an enemy that came in contact cannot damage the monster, Fear — it cannot damage anyone, Anger — in contact it may only attack and damage the monster, each until it visits its tower (its entry hex); Domination — an enemy in contact loses one action per turn; Petrify — an enemy in contact is locked for the rest of the turn; Mists — adjacent enemies cannot Attack.

Two copies = one id + a count, so every Set-by-id reader (Rule 24 candidatesOf / permStats via element_cost, hasPerm, Delay-Time-style readers of permanents_csv, the perms strip, dropPermanent, heldCards) stays correct: Rule 24 destroying it takes ONE copy (dropPermanent decrements and moves that copy's held card to the ARCHIVE — out of circulation, user answer 2026-11-15; the last copy drops the permanent). data.text: A character (a player's hero, a HUMAN profile hero, a team ally - never a summon or a monster) whose game falls silent for silence_ms becomes UNATTENDED: one live hero's game (the live hero with the smallest peer id) starts it again as a computer-operated peer with the same character, name, side, tile, class, stats and current life. It plays like an allied bot (attacks, moves, casts, abilities). With no master it holds its ground: it fights or casts at enemies in reach and does not roam. A human player of its link group (characters connected through ally joins - X joined next to Y as its ally - on the same side) becomes the group's MASTER: the earliest such join, ties by peer id. Leadership is sticky: while the master is alive and live a newer joiner does not take it; if the master dies or goes silent the group is leaderless until a player of the group is chosen again. Unattended characters with a master follow it like a summon (they walk to its side from anywhere, fighting what they meet in contact). When the owner comes back (rejoin, restore or any join of that character into that dimension) it takes the unattended character over - its life, its tile - and leaves the master's group. Killed while unattended = dead there; its death card goes to the killer. An unattended character with no other living character (its master counts) within vanish_radius hexes for vanish_after_ms leaves the dimension: no death, no card, it is no longer alive there.

logic.description: User ruling 2026-11-16 (revised): heroes without owner (character_id, no owner_peer_id) silent for data.unattended.silence_ms (120000; env SHADOW_MS shortens it for tests) become unattended: peer.mjs - run by the live hero with the smallest peer id, never by an unattended one - spawns an ordinary peer process (spawnCompanion wild, no owner) with SHADOW_OF = the hero's peer id, REPLACES_PEER_ID = the silent peer, ALLY_OF = its ally-join link, CHARACTER_ID / ENTITY_NAME / ALLIANCE / FORCE_CLASS / START_LIFE / SHADOW_STATS_JSON from its last snapshot, on its tile. It is not HUMAN: npcPlan plays it as an allied bot. Master (unattendedLeader): a group mate's live master is kept (sticky), else the live, alive human character of its link group (ally_of edges, same side) with the earliest joined_at (tie: peer id); published as led_by (followers) and leader (master). With a master npcPlan uses the summon owner-follow branch (walk next to it, fight what is in contact); without one it holds: npcCast / fight in contact, else Posture / Block. Takeover: the returning player (restore-here / restore / rejoin / a unit-list join of that profile character) boots with REPLACES_PEER_ID = the unattended peer and its life, ALLY_OF empty (it leaves the group); killed = dead there (death card: shadow_death, game/shadow-settle.mjs). Vanish: no living attended character (or its master) within data.unattended.vanish_radius for data.unattended.vanish_after_ms (env UNATTENDED_VANISH_MS for tests) -> it publishes out, pushes its Door and exits; receivers drop it, join-plan.mjs doorRecords drops out records (no longer alive there).

data.text: Dimension Out: a character may leave the dimension by channelling for `rounds` rounds (one round = one turn of three actions). The countdown shows on the unit for everyone. Moving, attacking or casting an effect interrupts it, as it interrupts any cast; taking damage does not, and the character can be killed meanwhile (then it is simply dead). When the countdown ends the character leaves cleanly: it is no longer in that dimension (not alive there, no unattended copy, no death card) and may join another dimension.

logic.description: User request 2026-11-16: peer.mjs dimOutStart (HUD 'dim_out' message, DIM_OUT_ON_START=1 from the start screen's restore-here + Dimension Out, bots only with SWARM_DIMOUT=1) sets dim_out_until_turn = turn + data.dimension_out.rounds (env DIM_OUT_ROUNDS for tests), published in the snapshot (every UI counts it down on the unit). doPlanningEnd cancels it when the action played is a move off the hex (M / EM), an attack (A) or an effect cast (data.dimension_out.interrupted_by); damage does not; death ends it. At turn >= dim_out_until_turn: leaveDimension — snapshot + Door `out`, the process exits; join-plan.mjs drops out records (not alive there, free for another dimension), no unattended copy, no death card.
